extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, patent practitioners, and patent applicants (owners/assignees/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on preparing, filing, processing, and withdrawing statutory and terminal disclaimers in U.S. patent applications and patents, including signature, content, timing, processing, and enforceability rules. Covers special situations (double patenting, joint research agreements, eTerminal Disclaimers, continuing applications, and post-issuance limitations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of disclaimers — statutory vs terminal
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two types of disclaimers: a statutory disclaimer (relinquishes legal rights to one or more claims of an issued patent) and a terminal disclaimer (disclaims or dedicates to the public the entire term, or any terminal part of the term, of a patent or patent to be granted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The historical usage distinguishes statutory disclaimers as disclaimers of claims of an issued patent and terminal disclaimers as disclaimers of patent term or a terminal part thereof. Both are provided for by statute, but are used differently; e.g., a statutory disclaimer cannot be used to amend or add claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory disclaimer content and recordation requirements (37 CFR 1.321(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A statutory disclaimer to be recorded in the Office must: (1) be signed by the patentee or an attorney/agent of record; (2) identify the patent and complete claim(s) or term being disclaimed (a disclaimer which is not of a complete claim or term will be refused recordation); (3) state the present extent of patentee's ownership interest in the patent; and (4) be accompanied by the required fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A statutory disclaimer is binding upon the grantee and its successors or assigns; notice is published in the Official Gazette and attached to printed specification copies. A statutory disclaimer is not a vehicle for adding or amending claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer content and recordation requirements (37 CFR 1.321(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A terminal disclaimer to be recorded must: (1) be signed by the applicant or an attorney/agent of record; (2) specify the portion of the term of the patent being disclaimed; (3) state the present extent of applicant's ownership interest in the patent to be granted; and (4) be accompanied by the required fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terminal disclaimers are binding upon the grantee and successors/assigns. The disclaimer must be of a terminal portion of the term of the entire patent to be granted — disclaimers of the term of individual claims are not accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer to obviate judicially created nonstatutory double patenting (37 CFR 1.321(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: When filed to obviate judicially created double patenting in an application or reexamination (except as provided in 1.321(d)), the terminal disclaimer must comply with provisions (b)(2)-(b)(4), be signed per applicable paragraph, and include a provision that any patent granted on that application (or subject to reexamination) shall be enforceable only during such period that it is commonly owned with the application or patent which formed the basis for the judicially created double patenting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terminal disclaimers filed under 1.321(c) are commonly used to overcome nonstatutory double patenting rejections; examiners should ensure the target application or patent is correctly identified before withdrawing the rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer for references disqualified due to joint research agreements (37 CFR 1.321(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A terminal disclaimer filed to obviate double patenting based on a patent or application disqualified as prior art under 1.104(c)(4)(ii) or (c)(5)(ii) (resulting from activities within scope of a joint research agreement) must: comply with (b)(2)-(b)(4); be signed per the applicable paragraph; and include a provision waiving the right to separately enforce any patent granted on the application (or subject to reexamination) and the reference patent, and that the patent(s) shall be enforceable only when they are not separately enforced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This special form of terminal disclaimer requires express waiver language and enforceability limitations; ensure the required waiver and enforcement wording are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirements — who may sign a disclaimer
rubrics_metrics.description: Signatures must be by the authorized party: patentee (assignee or inventor where not assigned), applicant, assignee in certain circumstances, or an attorney/agent of record. A registered practitioner acting solely in a representative capacity under 37 CFR 1.34 is not permitted to sign a disclaimer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signature rules vary by context (patent vs application, pre-AIA vs post-AIA filing date). When an attorney/agent of record signs, compliance with 37 CFR 3.73 is not required. Examiners and filers must check applicable signature rules for the filing date and proceeding type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant/ownership requirements — entirety of ownership must sign to obviate NSDP
rubrics_metrics.description: To obviate a nonstatutory double patenting rejection, the entirety of ownership must sign the terminal disclaimer disclaiming with respect to the reference on which the rejection is based, or multiple terminal disclaimers so disclaiming must be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an applicant who is not the owner (e.g., inventor who assigned away rights) signs, the terminal disclaimer will not be entered and the NSDP rejection will not be withdrawn. If only part ownership signs, a disclaimer from remaining owners is required. Ensure ownership interest is stated in the disclaimer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-AIA assignee signature and 37 CFR 3.73(b) compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an assignee signs a terminal disclaimer in a pre-AIA application, compliance with pre-AIA 37 CFR 3.73(b) is required unless an attorney/agent of record signs. To satisfy 3.73(b), either submit documentary evidence of chain of title or specify where such evidence is recorded in the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A statement of assignee interest (e.g., 'A and B are the owners of 100% of the instant application') is sufficient to satisfy pre-AIA 1.321(b)(3). Examiners may direct applicants to MPEP §324 and provide the Statement Under 37 CFR 3.73(b) as a form of compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: eTerminal Disclaimer (eTD) eligibility and auto-processing
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO web-based eTD can be used for pending nonprovisional utility applications (including national stage and reissue) and pending design applications; an eTD can include up to 50 reference applications and 50 reference patents and, if it meets all requirements, is auto-processed and approved immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An eTD may only be used if (1) inventor(s) named as applicant(s) own 100% of entire right, title and interest; (2) assignee/obligated assignee named as applicant owns 100%; or (3) a combination of inventor(s) and partial assignee(s) named as applicants together own 100%. eTDs are not accepted for plant patent applications, reexaminations, or joint research agreement-based disclaimers (those must be paper or scanned PDF).

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing of non-eTD terminal disclaimers (paper/scanned) in Technology Centers
rubrics_metrics.description: Paper or scanned terminal disclaimers filed in an application pending in a TC are processed by a Paralegal Specialist of the Patent Legal Research Center who: (A) determines compliance with 35 U.S.C. 253 and 37 CFR 1.321 and 3.73 and fee payment; (B) notifies the examiner whether the terminal disclaimer is acceptable; and (C) where not acceptable, indicates the nature of informalities so the examiner can inform applicant in the next Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paralegal completes a Terminal Disclaimer review decision form to notify the examiner of informalities. Paralegal approval is not an indication that the terminal disclaimer correctly identifies the target application/patent — the examiner must determine correct identification before withdrawing NSDP rejection(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirements for proper terminal disclaimer language
rubrics_metrics.description: A proper terminal disclaimer must disclaim the terminal part of the statutory term of any patent granted on the application (or the statutory term of the patent) which would extend beyond the expiration date of the full statutory term, shortened by any terminal disclaimer, of the patent that is the basis of the NSDP. It must state that the agreement runs with any patent granted on the application and is binding upon the grantee, its successors or assigns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissible exculpatory language (e.g., 'In making the above disclaimer, the owner does not disclaim...') may be used. The disclaimer should identify the disclaimant and their interest and specify the effective date. A terminal disclaimer of individual claim term is improper; conditional disclaimers (tied to PTA determinations, litigation outcomes, etc.) are not acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of terminal disclaimers on patent term adjustment (35 U.S.C. 154(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing a terminal disclaimer may affect any patent term adjustment provided under 35 U.S.C. 154(b): 'No patent the term of which has been disclaimed beyond a specified date may be adjusted under this section beyond the expiration date specified in the disclaimer.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be made aware that disclaiming part of the patent term can limit later PTA adjustments; examiners and paralegals should note potential PTA consequences when processing a terminal disclaimer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing requirements — disclaimers filed after payment of issue fee but before grant
rubrics_metrics.description: Any terminal disclaimer submitted after the date of payment of the issue fee but prior to the patent grant date must include a certificate of correction requesting that the face of the patent be amended to state that the patent is subject to a terminal disclaimer, unless the face of the patent already includes that language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a terminal disclaimer is filed after issue fee payment, include the certificate of correction to ensure proper printing on title page and asterisk placement. eTDs submitted after issue fee but prior to grant must follow same certificate requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer filed after expiration of reference patent is ineffective to obviate NSDP
rubrics_metrics.description: A terminal disclaimer filed under 37 CFR 1.321(c) or (d) after the expiration of the reference patent is not effective to obviate a nonstatutory double patenting rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts (e.g., Boehringer Ingelheim Int’l v. Barr Laboratories) have held that retroactive disclaimers filed after expiration would allow unjustified timewise extension and are therefore ineffective. Ensure terminal disclaimers intended to obviate NSDP are filed before the reference patent expiration if relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of terminal disclaimers in continuing applications, reexamination, and reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: A terminal disclaimer filed to obviate an NSDP rejection is effective only with respect to the application or patent identified in the disclaimer unless by its terms it extends to continuing applications (in which case applicant must file a copy of the disclaimer in the continuing application). A terminal disclaimer filed in a parent normally has no effect on a continuing application claiming benefits under 35 U.S.C. 120 unless properly extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must file copies of the disclaimer in continuing applications to achieve the intended carryover. Examiners should check whether a terminal disclaimer should be filed or has effect in related/progeny applications and CPAs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal/nullification of recorded terminal disclaimers — pre-issuance vs post-issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: A recorded terminal disclaimer may be withdrawn if a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 is granted before the application issues as a patent, or if filed in a reexamination proceeding before the reexamination certificate issues. After a patent or reexamination certificate issues, a recorded terminal disclaimer will not be nullified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a continuing application (other than a CPA) while abandoning the application with the terminal disclaimer may nullify effect; an RCE will not. Certificates of correction, reissue, or reexamination are generally not available to withdraw a recorded terminal disclaimer after issuance. Applicants may file explanatory papers and additional disclaimers to correct errors in named patents/applications or owner names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on using disclaimers to add or amend claims or as conditional instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: A statutory disclaimer or terminal disclaimer is not a vehicle for adding or amending claims; the statute and rules provide no mechanism to add claims via disclaimer. The statute does not provide for conditional disclaimers — proposed disclaimers contingent on PTA determinations, litigation outcomes, allowance of certain claims, or grant of a petition are improper and will not be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should refuse recordation of disclaimers that attempt to add/modify claims or are conditional. Applicants must use proper claim amendment procedures rather than disclaimers to change claim scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificates of Correction Branch responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Certificates of Correction Branch processes all statutory disclaimers filed under 35 U.S.C. 253(a) and 37 CFR 1.321 and all terminal disclaimers filed under 35 U.S.C. 253(b) and 37 CFR 1.321, except terminal disclaimers filed in pending applications or reexamination proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific branch tasks include: (A) determining compliance with statutes/rules; (B) notifying applicant or patentee when disclaimer is not acceptable; (C) recording disclaimers in application file; (D) providing statutory and terminal disclaimer data for Official Gazette printing; and (E) providing certificates of correction when necessary to amend patent face for terminal disclaimers entered during pendency but not printed on the title page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms and form selection depending on application filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO terminal disclaimer forms are available: Forms PTO/AIA/25 and PTO/AIA/26 for applications filed on or after September 16, 2012; Forms PTO/SB/25 and PTO/SB/26 for applications filed before that date; Forms PTO/SB/25a and PTO/SB/26a may be used in patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners and applicants may attach sample terminal disclaimer language (form paragraphs) in Office actions. The filing date of the application determines which form should be used.
